executiveSummary.reason: All 22 runtime passes still lack reliable human confirmation of audio, key, vocals, lyric timing, transitions, completeness, and presentation. They remain C-tier review candidates; runtime playback alone is not enough for S/A/B or production inclusion.

reconciledUniverse.calculation: 69 prior distinct candidates + 16 new exact video IDs first appearing in persisted v6-v11 candidate manifests = 85. The v5 Donna Cruz and Men Oppose IDs were already in the prior 69; their runtime state was corrected from pending to PASS using tools/medley-expansion-runtime-v5.json.

verifier.rootCause: The audit page treated a long initial YouTube BUFFERING state as a probable autoplay-policy failure after a 12-second grace period. In v9 sample-029 reached onReady and buffering, but PLAYING arrived only after the cutoff in two independent runs. The third run did play and passed. This made the control gate too sensitive to delayed startup, not evidence that candidate videos were playable.
correction: Classify startup from the observed official player state: buffering, paused, ended, or not-started; do not infer autoplay policy from the absence of PLAYING alone.
Increase startup grace from 12 to 20 seconds and default per-song timeout from 45 to 60 seconds.

Keep the PASS rule unchanged: matching video identity, onReady, PLAYING, and at least 15 seconds of sustained currentTime progression with qualifying advancing samples. READY or PLAYING without progression is never PASS.

proof.focusedRegressionTest: tests/playability-audit.test.mjs covers buffering not being mislabeled as autoplay failure.
proof.controlsAcrossValidCandidateBatches: 27/27 independent sample-029 runs passed the three-run gate.
proof.allPersistedControlRuns: 31 PASS / 2 CONTROL FAILURE across 33 recorded control runs; the two failures are the original v9 short-grace attempts.

invalidAttemptsPreserved.reason: Two controls did not reach PLAYING within the old 12-second startup grace; the batch stopped before candidate tests.

The runner had the candidate manifest, but its local browser page was not given --page-manifest and therefore showed the default production report. Candidate rows were absent; no candidate result is valid. The corrected v13 run loaded the candidate manifest and tested both candidates.

runtimeResults.passDefinition: Actual KantaCue player/controller, loaded identity matched, onReady, PLAYING, sustained currentTime advancement >=15 seconds.

deduplicationAndQualityDecisions.exactSectionsPolicy: Only description/list evidence is recorded. Blank section lists remain unknown; no sections were inferred by listening or from thumbnails.

verifiedFacts: Public video view totals and publication dates where captured in persisted evidence.
Runtime statuses from actual KantaCue YouTube IFrame player traces.
strongInferences: Multi-million-view medleys demonstrate established reach; high views accumulated over a shorter publication period are stronger qualitative momentum signals than old lifetime totals, but snapshots are not synchronized.
unknown: Google/YouTube search volume, current search rank, comprehensive recent view velocity, watch time, audience geography, audio quality, mix quality, key, guide vocals, sync, transition quality, and visual polish unless a human actually reviews the video.
demandMethodology.methodLimit: Public view snapshots come from different capture dates. No precise age-normalized ranking is presented as if measurements were contemporaneous. View count is not search volume or a quality override.

providerResearch.providerCaveat: Provider reputation is only a discovery clue; runtime/quality decisions are per video. Some channels show mixed outcomes; some providers in this sample returned only Error 150. This sample is not a universal provider ranking.

productionDecision.reason: No candidate can receive S/A/B evidence without human listening/presentation review. Keep all 22 technical PASS candidates outside production pending review; reject all Error 150 candidates and do not lower gates.

limitations: No human audio listening or presentation inspection was performed; all runtime-pass records remain C-tier.
Headless Chrome playback proves technical progression for the tested session, not future availability, all-region behavior, or user-device performance.
No reliable search-volume data was available; search-demand labels remain UNKNOWN.
Most candidate track lists are unknown unless captured from a public video description; no lyric text is stored.
Exact 1080p or consistent HD quality was not verified.
The full adversarial UX/PWA checks are covered by the existing application regression suite but were not manually re-exercised at every viewport in this metadata-only expansion pass.
